messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PAGE: infer-prod GPU pool queue depth exceeded critical threshold (avg queue=1240, 95p latency > 2.5s) — paging alice (oncall). Incident ID: INC-2026-0419-01

alice (oncall): ack. I'm looking. Any customer-facing alerts yet?

dave (prodops): seeing sustained enqueue rate ~11k reqs/min against pool capacity of 12 GPUs. Autoscaler didn't add nodes after hitting scale-cap=14. Metric: pool_scale_attempts=0 since 10:12 UTC.

carmen (eng-runtime): fyi we rolled batch-config v2.3.1 ~09:58 UTC — it tightened continuous batching window from 80ms -> 12ms and changed prefix cache TTL from 30m -> 60s in attempt to reduce tail latency. That looks suspicious.

ben (sre): logs show many small batches now -> lower batch utilization, more per-token overhead. Also prefix cache missrate jumped: prefix_cache_hitrate=0.11 (was 0.89 pre-rollout).

remy (support): two accounts reported throttled requests (~10 customers) — support ticket volume rising. I told them we're investigating and to route high-priority customers to remy@.

alice (oncall): prioritized mitigation options? Can we increase pool or temporarily disable the new batch params?

carmen (eng-runtime): recommend rollback of batch-config v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 and bump prefix_cache TTL back. Rollback path is tested: apply config via infra-config and autoscaler will re-evaluate.

dave (prodops): I'm wary of full rollback impact on latency — alternative quick mitigation: temporarily lift scale_cap to 18 for infer-prod and force a scale-out. That will buy headroom while we rollback.

ben (sre): to be safe, do both: lift scale_cap + rollback. I'll run the commands.

ben (sre): running: 
```
# lift scale cap
infractl pools update infer-prod --scale-cap 18 --reason "incident INC-2026-0419-01 emergency"
# trigger scale
infractl pools trigger-scale infer-prod --target-gpus 16
```

pagerbot: infractl action accepted. scale_cap updated, scale job queued.

alice (oncall): Carmen, please prepare rollback PR and config patch. Dave/Ben coordinate scale. Remy, prepare customer comms: short blurb and ETA. Linda, are there any enterprise customers on dedicated capacity impacted?

linda (customer-success): Only one enterprise trial (acme-corp) hit throttling; they've escalated to CS. CS on call now with ACME rep. We'll send an interim note: "We're actively mitigating a capacity issue affecting some inference requests; we expect partial recovery within ~20–30m."

carmen (eng-runtime): patch ready. Pushing rollback:
```
git checkout -b rollback/batchconfig-v2.3.0
git revert -m 1 <commit-sha-of-v2.3.1>
./deploy-config infra-config/prod/infer-prod/batch-config.yaml
```

carmen (eng-runtime): deploy started (deploy-id: deploy-22776-rc1). Rolling patch to 3/6 serving nodes now.

ben (sre): autoscaler logs show failed scale decisions due to actuator rate limit at 10/min — looks like a separate throttling guard tripped by the automated scale flood. I've disabled the actuator rate-limiter for infer-prod temporarily: `autoscalerctl set-guard infer-prod actuator-rate-limit 0`

pagerbot: NOTE: guard removed by ben (sre).

alice (oncall): good. Monitor queue and prefix cache hitrate. Key metrics to watch: queue_depth, p95_latency, prefix_cache_hitrate, batch_size_avg, gpu_util.

(approx +8 minutes)
ben (sre): scale-out progressing. GPUs provisioned -> 14 active now. queue_depth -> 610 (was 1240). p95_latency -> 1.8s

carmen (eng-runtime): rollback completed on all nodes. prefix_cache TTL restored to 30m. prefix_cache_hitrate -> 0.78 and climbing. batch_size_avg -> 12.9 (pre-rollout baseline ~13.6)

remy (support): sending customer update: "We've partially mitigated the issue; capacity increased and config rollback in progress. You may see degraded latency for a short period. We'll follow up when fully resolved."

alice (oncall): any SLO breaches? Estimate: current daily error budget burn rate spiking. We need to track if any customers hit SLA. Ben, can you run a query for 5m error counts and throttled responses?

ben (sre): query run: `SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE response_code=429 AND pool='infer-prod' AND ts > now()-5m` -> 342 throttled in last 5m. Most between 10:05–10:20 UTC.

linda (customer-success): ACME CS notified. They want postmortem and timeline. Assigning follow-up owner: carmen + ben for root cause and mitigation doc.

alice (oncall): short-term status: degraded but stabilizing. We're keeping scale cap lifted to 18 for 1h, monitoring. Action items:
- ben: monitor and revert actuator guard back to normal after steady-state (ticket SRE-INC-2277654321)
- carmen: root-cause writeup (batching param change + prefix TTL change) and a plan to gate batch-config rollouts with synthetic load tests
- dave: confirm cost impact for emergency scale and coordinate finance notice if > $Xk
- remy/linda: customer comms and targeted outreach to impacted customers

(approx +47 minutes)
ben (sre): queue_depth stable ~80, p95_latency < 600ms, prefix_cache_hitrate 0.86. Autoscaler healthy; I'll reduce scale-cap back to 14 in 30m if no regressions.

alice (oncall): handing off to night oncall @dave. I'm going offline but available by phone. Handoff notes: rollback done, scale cap 18 (temp), actuator guard disabled (monitoring), customers notified. Pager channel will remain open.

dave (prodops): ack taking over. I'll keep the cap at 16 now and watch for flapping. If anything spikes, I'll page SRE.

pagerbot: Incident INC-2026-0419-01 status -> mitigated (partial). Pages silenced for 30m.

remy (support): updating support tickets with mitigation timeline and next steps for follow-up.

carmen (eng-runtime): postmortem draft assigned to me + ben. Will include timeline, root cause (regression in batch-config v2.3.1), why prefix cache TTL change caused cache warm cold-start, and an action to require canary synthetic load tests for batch-config changes.

alice (oncall): closing notes: customers impacted: ~10 accounts, ~350 throttled responses in peak window, ACME escalated. Next: PM/SE meeting for rollout policy change. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
